name: Car-free access ranking
description: US cities ranked by how much of the job market you can reach without a car.

meta.dataSource: Whole-network job-access ranking: the transit data pipeline web/*_runreport.json, field scenarios[].summary.transit_job_access_percapita (+ jobs_within_45min_transit, transit_pct) — table `cities` (still drives the standalone Map tab) and mode=all rows of `citymode`. The original 5 cities (Boston, Chicago, Seattle, Toronto, Glasgow) use scenarios[0] '2019 baseline'; the 28 cities pulled 2026-07-12 from the production server ship a DIFFERENT scenario set (2010/2019/2030/2040/2050) with no index-0 '2019 baseline' label, so those rows use the scenario whose label contains '2019' (labeled '2019 (present)' — same real year, different label text; each row's own scenario_label field states which). Per-mode network coverage + frequency: the transit data pipeline web/carfree_modes.json, produced by the build script (pure stdlib GTFS parser; method + 500m walk-buffer approximation documented in the data-sources ledger) — table `citymode`, one row per (city, mode in {all,bus,tram,subway,rail}); mode=all rows carry the SAME ranking numbers as `cities`, per-mode rows carry ONLY network stats, never an access number. v2 (2026-07-12) = 33 cities in the ranking; only the original 4 (Boston, Chicago, Seattle, Toronto — no local GTFS pulled for any of the other 29 including Glasgow) have per-mode rows; the 28 new cities are mode=all only, per-mode fields left null/blank (rendered '-', never 0), Glasgow-style. v4 (2026-07-31, seedVersion .1-carfree-t2-cities, roadmap unit T2): added local GTFS feeds for 5 more ranked cities (New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Atlanta, Portland) — their `cities`/mode=all access numbers are untouched, only per-mode network rows were added/filled. Plus Helsinki as a 34th `citymode`-only city (network rows, no access model run yet, absent from `cities`/the ranking — see T7). New York/San Francisco/Los Angeles feeds are single-agency rail/subway-only (MTA subway, BART, LA Metro rail respectively) — their per-mode NETWORK stats (not access numbers) are rail/subway-only, stated in each row's method_note and in the About screen. `citymode` is the single seeded feed driving BOTH the Ranking screen's cards and its inline map (board-level mode filter reshapes both); append more rows to add cities (see the internal notes for the exact pull command).
meta.scoreMethod: v3 (2026-07-12, seedVersion .5-carfree-dualscale): BOTH scales are seeded on every mode=all row, switchable via two UI tabs. score_log = LOG-scale normalize of transit_job_access_percapita across the FULL seeded city set (33 cities): round(100*(ln(x)-ln(min))/(ln(max)-ln(min)),1), min city = 0, max city = 100 — the readable comparison, since New York/London are ~10x access outliers that a plain linear scale compresses everyone else under (e.g. Chicago would read 2.8 and look flatly 'car-needed' despite real transit; on the log scale it reads 37.0). score_linear = plain min-max normalize of the same number: round(100*(x-min)/(max-min),1) — the raw spread, showing exactly how far ahead New York (100) and London (~83.4) truly are (Washington ~18.9, Boston ~10.1, Chicago ~2.8, min city 0). The plain `score` column mirrors score_log for any older binding. Both preserve the SAME rank order (only the score's spread changes, never who's ahead). Tier bands (excellent/good/fair/car-needed) are assigned from score_log ONLY, on both tabs, at fixed cutoffs: excellent >=65, good >=45, fair >=25, car-needed below 25 — chosen so NYC/London plus the genuinely strong pack (Washington, Montreal, San Francisco) read excellent/good, and weak-transit cities still read honestly low, without absurd outcomes like Chicago landing in car-needed. Both scales re-normalize automatically as more cities are appended, so scores (not ranks) will keep shifting as the set grows. Applies ONLY to mode=all rows — per-mode rows are unscored network-coverage stats.
